title: Empirical formula
body: The empirical formula is the chemical formula that lists the lowest whole number ratio of atoms of the elements in a compound.
ced_evidence: 1.3.A.3 "lowest whole number ratio of atoms of the elements in a compound is the empirical formula"

title: Coulomb's law
ced_evidence: 1.5.A.2 "EQN: Fcoulombic ∝ q1q2/r^2"; used qualitatively in 1.5.A.4 and 1.7.A.2

title: Bond likelihood from valence electrons and nuclei
body: Whether two elements will form a chemical bond is determined by the interactions between the valence electrons and the nuclei of the elements.
ced_evidence: 1.8.A.1 "determined by the interactions between the valence electrons and nuclei of elements"

title: Tools for explaining periodic trends
body: Periodic trends in atomic properties are qualitatively understood using these four ideas, in the CED's order.

items.label: Coulomb's law
items.meaning: The force between charged particles is proportional to q1q2/r^2.

items.label: Shell model
items.meaning: Electrons are arranged in shells (energy levels) and subshells (sublevels).

items.label: Shielding
items.meaning: Other electrons reduce the nuclear attraction felt by an electron.

items.label: Effective nuclear charge
items.meaning: The net positive charge of the nucleus experienced by an electron after shielding.

ced_evidence: 1.7.A.2 "qualitatively understood using Coulomb's law, the shell model, and the concepts of shielding and effective nuclear charge"
